主要内容: General Electric (GE) shares rose 7.76% on Tuesday following the announcement of its plan to spin off its health-care unit. The move is part of a broader strategy to refocus GE's operations on aviation, power, and renewable energy businesses. CEO John Flannery stated that the company will maintain its current quarterly dividend until the spinoff is completed and then adjust it in line with industrial peers. Flannery also mentioned that the company is likely to lower its aggregate dividend once the health-care spinoff is finished. GE also plans to reduce its net debt by about $25 billion by 2020 and generate $500 million or more in corporate cost savings by the end of 2020. Moody's Investors Service reaffirmed its A2 rating for GE but maintained a negative outlook for its debt due to expected continued weakness in earnings and cash flows through 2019 and into 2020. The company will also fully separate its stake in Baker Hughes, a GE company (BHGE). GE’s Board of Directors unanimously approved the plan, which includes separating GE Healthcare into a standalone company and pursuing an orderly separation from BHGE over the next two to three years. John Flannery, chairman and CEO of GE, emphasized that the spin-off would create a pure-play healthcare company and a tier-one oil and gas servicing and equipment player. GE also aims to reduce its industrial net debt by approximately $25 billion by 2020 and maintain more than $15 billion of cash on the balance sheet. The new GE Operating System will result in a smaller corporate headquarters focused on strategy, capital allocation, talent, and governance. GE expects to maintain its current quarterly dividend until GE Healthcare is established as an independent entity. Kieran Murphy, president and CEO of GE Healthcare, will continue to lead the unit as a standalone company, maintaining the GE brand.
